newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa consolidating, chance of push higher.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa consolidating, chance of push higher.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Cocoa futures are likely to go on consolidating, with a chance they will move higher for another try at nearby resistance around the 1,060 stg level, analysts said.
Traders called cocoa to open around four sterling down.
Having pushed back above the psychological support level at 1,000 stg, cocoa was in a consolidation phase, Susan Rigg, analyst at Chart Analysis said.
After such a big fall from its highs, it was unlikely to head back up to the peaks in the short term.
There was a chance it would push back up to the key 1,060 stg a tonne resistance level.
"With luck it'll trade sideways to up," Rigg said. "Without luck it'll trade sideways to down."
New York cocoa futures ended firmer in subdued dealings on Friday, but prices drifted off session highs on scattered mixed selling, dealers said.
"It was very, very quiet," said one trader. "It was a big move, but on no volume. Nobody can put a finger on this market because it's moving on no volume at all."
The president of the National Association of Cocoa Producers estimated that Mexico's 1996-97 harvest will end between 50,000 and 55,000 tonnes.

In an interview with Reuters, Laurence Rodriguez Torruco said his estimates were based on the production to date of 36,000 tonnes in the cycle's March-October harvesting period and favourable weather.
